title: Today's white paper - implications for PD
author: Dr Haili Hughes
summary: Reading the DfE's new white paper 'Every child achieving and thriving' (published 23 February 2026) through a professional-development lens, Hughes argues it functions as a system design document for how capability will be built across teachers, leaders and trusts. She highlights the new Teacher Training Entitlement as the most explicit policy lever, intended to ensure every teacher and leader can access high-quality PD, and traces its implications across five areas: inclusion/SEND becoming a mainstream workforce expectation (backed by over £200 million for SEND CPD), NPQ reform pushing leadership development toward 'people leadership', a shift toward networked professional learning via RISE hubs and alliances, engagement and belonging entering the PD curriculum alongside pedagogy, and AI/data capability moving from fringe CPD to core professional judgement frameworks. She closes with four practical threads leaders should build around: career-stage entitlement, inclusion as default, engagement/attendance/culture capability, and networked improvement.
points: Hughes reframes a government policy document as a 'system design paper' for workforce capability, translating dense white paper language into concrete implications for PD leaders.
She flags the Teacher Training Entitlement's explicit link to AI and technology as a signal that trusts must move beyond ad hoc 'AI twilight sessions' toward a genuine capability pathway.

Her point that SEND/inclusion is shifting from a specialist strand to 'the spine of PD', backed by over £200 million in funding, reframes inclusion as a mainstream workforce expectation rather than a SENCO-only responsibility.

Her four practical threads (career-stage entitlement, inclusion as default, engagement/culture capability, networked improvement) give leaders an actionable checklist rather than leaving the policy analysis abstract.
quotes: The new DfE white paper, Every child achieving and thriving, is not just a schools reform document. Read through a professional development lens, it is really a system design paper for how capability will be built across teachers, leaders, support staff, schools and trusts.

The most explicit policy lever is the new Teacher Training Entitlement (TTE), which the paper says is intended to ensure every teacher and leader can access high-quality professional development... the TTE will evolve to support evidence-based practice, including the use of technology and AI.

One of the strongest implications in the white paper is that SEND/inclusion capability is now a mainstream workforce expectation... announces over 200 million pounds over 3 years for a SEND CPD programme.
The white paper states that NPQs will be reformed to better reflect current training needs, including supporting children with SEND and people leadership skills.
For those leading PD at scale, this is less about promoting tools and more about creating professional judgement frameworks.
